title: Tesla's selective search: follow the choices

tesla_patent.title: US20260105614A1 — Artificial intelligence modeling techniques for joint behavior planning and forecasting
tesla_patent.supports: Tesla-assigned patent application published 2026-04-16. Describes hierarchical goal/interaction layers, node/trajectory scores, physics constraints, comfort, intervention likelihood, human-like discriminator, and threshold-based pruning. Does not mention HW3, V14 or an 80% performance figure.

tesla_fsd_support.supports: Currently enabled features require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous. Available features vary with configuration, hardware, software, region and model/year.

branching_math.text: Three independent choices at each of three stages produce 3, 9, then 27 possible sequences.

shots.title: Choose what deserves attention
shots.narration: Three choices: turn, creep forward, or wait. This example will show how a planner chooses where to spend effort. A pedestrian is crossing and an oncoming car is approaching. Our car waits. The other choices can still be represented, but they don't all deserve endless exploration. Tesla's patent application describes one way to make that search selective. First, watch what happens when we add just two more decision stages.
shots.teaches: Waiting is a candidate decision linked to the actual crossing and oncoming traffic.
shots.visual_intent: Begin inside a built-out 3D junction at car height; show the crossing, opposing vehicle, and three possible actions. Reveal waiting as the illustrative choice while the actors remain visible.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: Why three choices grow quickly
shots.narration: Those three choices are only the first stage. Give each one three follow-up choices. Now there are nine possible sequences. Add a third stage, and there are twenty-seven. Nothing complicated happened at any one step; the combinations did the growing. These are numbers in our simplified example, not a Tesla performance measurement. To compare useful futures, we need to connect each choice to a driving goal and the interactions that follow.
shots.teaches: Three alternatives at each of three stages produce 27 sequences in this example.
shots.visual_intent: Grow spatial layers from the detailed junction into three lit candidate worlds, then 9 and 27 bounded markers; reveal the count only after the viewer sees the expansion. No long empty floor view.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: Connect the decisions
shots.narration: The goal is the lane beyond the turn. Start there, then connect the possible interactions. Passing before another road user and waiting to pass behind them create different branches. A later choice depends on what happened earlier. That linked sequence is a candidate trajectory: one possible way of moving through the situation. The patent calls this a hierarchical graph. We can follow a route through it without pretending these graphics reproduce Tesla's software. But what happens to a road user outside the immediate conflict?
shots.teaches: A trajectory links dependent interactions to a goal rather than being an isolated line.
shots.visual_intent: Track one chain through spatial traffic states and return to the lane goal. Change angle to expose a dependency, rather than repeating the whole graph from a new orbit.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: The cyclist stays
shots.narration: The cyclist is off to the side. Does that mean the planner can forget about them? No. The cyclist stays in the scene. What can change is their relevance to the particular interaction we are considering. That is different from deleting the person or spending zero computation on them. If the situation changes, they may matter to the next decision. We still need a way to compare the choices that remain.
shots.teaches: Changing relevance to a candidate interaction does not justify ignoring the road user.
shots.visual_intent: Keep the cyclist fully rendered and moving. Dim only the candidate relationship; return to a street-level view so the distinction is visible.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: A useful choice has consequences
shots.narration: A possible turn can be physically feasible and still be abrupt or uncomfortable. Compare these two illustrative motions. The application describes scoring factors including physics-based constraints, comfort, intervention likelihood, and a human-like discriminator. Those factors help evaluate candidate behavior. We're showing the kinds of considerations involved, not Tesla's actual numeric scores or weights. A score is useful because it can guide what the planner develops next. Now watch what happens to a branch that falls below a threshold.
shots.teaches: Candidate evaluation can consider several behavior factors rather than an invented single score.
shots.visual_intent: Show a clearly labelled illustrative motion comparison and highlight the relevant factor as it is explained. Replace arbitrary pulsating score bars with a visible consequence; no invented Tesla weights.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: Pay off the pruning idea
shots.narration: The patent describes comparing node scores with a threshold and removing lower-scoring nodes. This is pruning. The poor branch stops growing, while a more promising branch develops more detail. Look back at the road: the pedestrian and cyclist are still there. We have removed a candidate from the search, not a person from the world. That can avoid work on trajectories that would not be selected. The method describes a way to focus effort. It does not give us a measured percentage saving for this example.
shots.teaches: Threshold pruning stops developing a poor candidate and directs expansion toward promising nodes.
shots.visual_intent: Tie the threshold to a specific branch; stop and retract that branch while the retained one gains detail. Maintain the pedestrian and cyclist in the underlying junction.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: Separate the hardware claim
shots.narration: Does more selective search make an older computer equivalent to a newer one? That does not follow from this application. Planning is one part of a system that also has perception, prediction, memory, and timing requirements. The document does not establish Hardware Three feature parity, version fourteen deployment, or an eighty-percent saving. Those need separate product evidence. Tesla describes Full Self-Driving Supervised as requiring active driver supervision, and says features vary with the vehicle's hardware and software. The useful check is to match a feature claim to an actual release for the actual vehicle.
shots.teaches: An application about planning does not establish deployment or feature parity for a specific hardware generation.
shots.visual_intent: Hold the generic hardware physically constant while the search changes. Distinguish the application from verified release evidence in a detailed technical set, with source identifiers available.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

shots.title: Test and apply the lesson
shots.narration: One last check. When a branch is pruned, what must remain represented? The road user. That distinction is the lesson: organize the choices, compare their consequences, and stop developing poor branches. Our car can finish the illustrated turn once the crossing and opposing lane are clear. We can understand the planning idea while keeping a hardware-upgrade claim separate.
shots.teaches: The viewer can distinguish pruning candidate decisions from losing representation of an agent.
shots.visual_intent: Briefly invite the viewer to locate the still-visible road user, reveal them clearly, then complete the illustrative left turn. End on the resolved driving situation rather than a repeated empty graph.
shots.simplifications: Illustrative driving states and scoring factors; not a Tesla implementation or measured benchmark.

opening.viewer_value: Follow the planning mechanism and separate it from an unsupported hardware-upgrade claim.
